pubchem.title: Linalool
pubchem.description: Linalool is a monoterpenoid that is octa-1,6-diene substituted by methyl groups at positions 3 and 7 and a hydroxy group at position 3. It has been isolated from plants like Ocimum canum. It has a role as a volatile oil component, an antimicrobial agent, a fragrance and a plant metabolite. It is a monoterpenoid and a tertiary alcohol.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Linalool is a naturally occurring monoterpenoid and tertiary alcohol that gives many flowers and spice plants their signature floral, slightly spicy scent. As a major component of volatile essential oils, it is widely used as a fragrance in perfumes and cosmetics. You likely encounter its sweet, calming aroma daily in everything from fresh herbs to scented soaps.
consumer_summary.found_in: This fragrant molecule is abundant in familiar culinary and medicinal plants, including basil (Ocimum basilicum), lavender (Lavandula angustifolia), coriander, and ginger. It is also a key aromatic component in citrus fruits like lemons and oranges, as well as in hops used for brewing.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to linalool for its broad potential as an antimicrobial agent and its prominent role in traditional calming botanicals like lavender. The scientific community is actively exploring how this fragrant molecule interacts with the nervous system and its ability to combat oxidative stress. The strongest evidence so far comes from individual randomised trials (Oxford level 1b) investigating its antimicrobial, antioxidant, and insect-repellent properties. If these diverse applications bear out, linalool could serve as a versatile foundation for new topical treatments and natural preservatives.

structure_function.statement: Linalool is being studied for its ability to support defenses against microbial growth.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 32 papers, including an individual randomised trial and several in vitro studies.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward linalool's potential to support cellular health by acting as an antioxidant.
structure_function.basis: This is supported by 22 papers, including one individual randomised trial and 11 animal studies.

structure_function.statement: Linalool may support natural insect-repellent formulations.
structure_function.basis: This is based on 11 papers, including an individual randomised trial and several animal models.

structure_function.statement: Researchers are exploring whether linalool may support a calm mood and ease feelings of anxiety.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 7 papers, including human observational research and animal studies.

structure_function.statement: Linalool is being studied for its potential to support pain relief and physical comfort.
structure_function.basis: This is supported by 5 papers, including human observational and animal research.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether linalool's calming aroma can directly improve sleep quality and reduce occupational burnout.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: This is currently being investigated in a completed clinical trial (NCT06914167) evaluating lavender aromatherapy combined with slow breathing exercises in nursing staff.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether linalool might influence cellular pathways related to tumor growth, which could eventually inform new supportive therapies.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial in human patients to evaluate a standardized linalool formulation alongside standard care, measuring tumor markers and quality of life over six months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early work points toward the possibility that linalool could help modulate the body's inflammatory response, potentially offering a soothing effect for localized flare-ups.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human trial applying a topical linalool preparation to localized inflammation, measuring inflammatory cytokine levels and patient-reported discomfort over four weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether linalool might support focus and memory by interacting with monoaminergic pathways in the brain.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: The next step would be a randomized, placebo-controlled human trial administering a controlled dose of linalool to healthy adults and measuring cognitive performance and memory retention over a 12-week period.

consumer_summary.cautions: When oxidized upon exposure to air, linalool forms hydroperoxides that are a known occupational exposure hazard and can cause allergic contact dermatitis.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far includes individual randomised trials (Oxford level 1b) for its antimicrobial, antioxidant, and insect-repellent properties, while research into its neurological and anti-inflammatory benefits remains largely at the human observational and animal stages.
